context: We presented the first data structure for preprocessed 3SUM with unknown C that has truly subquadratic space and query time (and quadratic preprocessing). We’ll discuss some possible extensions. 4.1 What do we get with optimal function inversion? The only known lower bounds for function inversion [25, 10, 15] give that the space S and query time T must satisfy ST ≥ Ω̃(N ). While a matching upper bound is only known for random permutations [19], it is conceivable that a construction achieving this bound might be possible for arbitrary functions as no higher lower bounds are known.

context: space n2−ε and query time n1.5+ε . 4.2 What tradeoff is desirable? A brute-force query algorithm would solve 3SUM on each query without the need for preprocessing. This would achieve space O(n) (just store A and B) and query time O(n2 )4 . Interpolating between this and the space-n2 and query-n1.5 trade-off of [22], one might hope to be able to achieve for every ε ∈ [0, 1/2], space n2−2ε and query time n1.5+ε . Unfortunately, even with optimal function inversion, our construction doesn’t achieve such a result. Either new ideas are needed, or perhaps there is some limitation to achieving such a tradeoff.
